<!-- defn-1: body_md -->
\label{def:K-of-matroid}
The $K$-theory spectrum $K(E,\mathcal F)$ of a matroid $M=(E,\mathcal F)$ is defined
to be the spectrum $K^{\mathrm{zar}}(X) \cong K'(X)$, where $X$ is
the toric monoid scheme associated to the Bergman fan of $M$.
We write $K'_n(M)$ for the homotopy group
$K'_n(X) = \pi_nK'(X)$.
<!-- end defn-1 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:comparison-intro}
Let $X$ be a toric monoid scheme, and $k$ a field.
Then the natural map of spectra is a weak homotopy equivalence:
\[
K(k)\wedge K' (X)\xrightarrow{\sim} K'(X_k)
\]
In particular, the realization map is an isomorphism:
\[ K'_0(X)\xrightarrow{\sim} K'_0(X_k). \]
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
Let $X$ be a smooth proper toric monoid scheme, and $k$ a field.
Then $K_0(X_k)$ is a free abelian group, independent of $k$,
and there are natural isomorphisms 
\[
\mu^X_n: K_0(X_k)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} \pi^s_n
= K_0(X_k)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(\mathbf{pt}) \xrightarrow{\sim} K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(X).
\]
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- ex-1: body_md -->
Let $A$ be the multiplicative monoid $\{0,1\}$, the initial object in the category of pointed
 commutative monoids. We write $\mathbf{pt} = \operatorname{MSpec}(A)$ for the associated monoid scheme, which is the final object in ${\mathcal M}_{\text{pctf}}$. We have $\mathbf{pt}_k = \operatorname{Spec} (k)$.
<!-- end ex-1 -->
<!-- defn-2: body_md -->
\label{def:TMS}  (\cite[4.1]{CHWW})
A {\it toric monoid scheme} is a separated, connected, torsionfree,
normal monoid scheme of finite type.
<!-- end defn-2 -->
<!-- defn-3: body_md -->
\label{fan-monoid-scheme}
Given a fan $(N,\Delta)$, we  define a contravariant functor $A$
from the poset $\Delta$ to monoids (written additively).
Set $M=\operatorname{Hom}(N,\mathbb{Z})$.  
For each cone $\sigma $ in $\Delta$, form the monoid (pointed by adding a base point $\ast$):
\[
A(\sigma) = (\sigma^\vee\cap M)_\ast, \quad \textrm{where} \quad
\sigma^\vee = \{m\in M_\mathbb{R}: m(\sigma)\ge0\}.
\]
If $\tau$ is a face of $\sigma$, there is $m\in A(\sigma)$
  such that  $A(\tau)$ is obtained from $A(\sigma)$ by inverting $m$.
  This implies that there is a prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}(\tau)$  of $A(\sigma)$
such that  $A(\tau)=A(\sigma)_{\mathfrak{p}(\tau)}$.
As observed in \cite[4.2]{CHWW}, $A$ is the stalk functor of
a toric monoid scheme $X(N,\Delta)$;
when $N$ is understood, we just write $X(\Delta)$.
<!-- end defn-3 -->
<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:smooth-monoid-scheme}
	A monoid scheme $X$ is {\it smooth} if it is cancellative and its $k$-realization $X_k$ is a smooth $k$-scheme for all fields $k$. As discussed in \cite[Sec.\,6]{CHWW}, this is equivalent to the property that every stalk
	 $\mathcal{O}_{X,x}$ is a smash product of a pointed free monoid and a pointed free abelian group. In particular, if $X$ is affine, then $X\cong \mathbb{A}^s\times \mathbb{G}_m^t$ for some $s,t\geq 0$.
<!-- end rem-1 -->
<!-- ex-2: body_md -->
Let $X = X(\Delta, N)$ be a toric monoid scheme. The reduced and irreducible equivariant closed subschemes of $X$ are in one-to-one correspondence with the cones of $\Delta$. If $k$ is a field, and $Y\subseteq X$ is a reduced and irreducible equivariant closed subscheme, then $Y_k$ is an orbit closure in the toric $k$-variety $X_k$.
<!-- end ex-2 -->
<!-- defn-4: body_md -->
\label{def:blowup}
Let $X$ be a monoid scheme of finite type and $Y \subseteq X$ an
equivariant closed subscheme, given by a quasi-coherent sheaf of monoid
ideals $\mathcal I$. The {\it blow-up} of $X$ along $Y$ is the
projective morphism $X_Y=\operatorname{MProj}(\mathcal{O}_X[\mathcal I t])\to X$.
If $k$ is a field, then $(X_Y)_k\to X_k$ is the
blow-up of the $k$-scheme $X_k$ along the closed subscheme $Y_k$.
<!-- end defn-4 -->
<!-- defn-5: body_md -->
The group $K'_0(X)$ may be defined as a Grothendieck group: the abelian
group generated by the classes $[Z]$ of sheaves of finitely generated
${\mathrm{pc}}$-sets, modulo the relations
that $[Z]=]Y]+[Z/Y]$ for every extension $Z\subset Y$;
	see \cite[2.1]{HW}
<!-- end defn-5 -->
<!-- ex-3: body_md -->
\label{ex:proj-space-K}
  $K'_0$ of the projective space $\mathbb{P}^n$ was computed in \cite[5.7]{HW}:
  $K'_0(\mathbb{P}^n)\cong \mathbb{Z}^{n+1}$ on the classes of the structure sheaves
  of the closed	subvarieties $\mathbb{P}^i$ ($i=0,...,n$). 
  It follows that the canonical map (induced by realization)
  $K'_0(\mathbb{P}^n) \to K'_0(\mathbb{P}^n_k)$ is an isomorphism for any field $k$.
<!-- end ex-3 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:K-loc}
	Let $X$ be a pc monoid scheme and $Z\,{\buildrel i \over \longrightarrow}\, X$ an equivariant closed subscheme
	with open complement $U\,{\buildrel j \over \longrightarrow}\, X$. Then there is a fibration sequence of connective spectra
	\[
	K'(Z)\,{\buildrel i_* \over \longrightarrow}\, K'(X) \,{\buildrel j^* \over \longrightarrow}\, K'(U).
	\]
In particular, the map $K'_0(X)\to K'_0(U)$ is onto.
<!-- end thm-3 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:K'-MV}
  Let $X$ be a pc monoid scheme and $U,\,V\subseteq X$
  open subschemes covering $X$. 
	Then there is a long exact Mayer--Vietoris sequence
\[
\dotsm \to K'_n(X)\to K'_n(U)\oplus K'_n(V)\to K'_n(U\cap V) \to K'_{n-1}(X)\to \dotsm
\]
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
This is a standard argument, see for example
  \cite[Prop.\,4]{BG} or \cite[V.6.11.2]{WK}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- rem-2: body_md -->
We also have $K'_0(X\times\mathbb{G}_{\text m})\simeq K'_0(X)$; see \cite[5.4]{HW}.
<!-- end rem-2 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:comparison}
Let $X$ be a toric monoid scheme, and $k$ a field.
Then the natural map of spectra 
\[ K(k)\wedge K' (X)\xrightarrow{\sim} K'(X_k) \]
is a weak homotopy equivalence. 
 
In particular, the realization map is an isomorphism:
\[ K'_0(X)\xrightarrow{\sim} K'_0(X_k). \]
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
We proceed by induction on the dimension $n$ of $X$.
  If $n = 0$, then $X$ is a point, and $K'(X)$ is the
  sphere spectrum $\mathbb{S}$. On the other hand,
  $X_k = \operatorname{Spec} (k)$, so $K'(X_k) = K'(k)$.
  The asserted equivalence follows. 
	
  Now assume that $n > 0$, and we have proved the assertion for all
  toric monoid schemes of dimension less than $n$. Since $X$ is a
  toric monoid scheme, there is a sequence of open subschemes 
\[
\operatorname{MSpec}(\mathbb{Z}_+^{\wedge t}) \cong X_0 \subset X_1 \subset \dotsm \subset X_t = X
\]
such that, for $0 < i\leq t$, $Z_i = X_i \setminus X_{i-1}$ is a toric
monoid scheme of dimension $i-1$ embedded as an equivariant closed
subscheme into $X_i$. The assertion of the theorem is true for $X_0$
by \cite[Thm.\,4.6]{HW} and the Fundamental Theorem of $K'$-theory
(see \cite[Section 6, Thm.\,8]{Quillen}). It also holds for the monoid
schemes $Z_i$ by the inductive hypothesis. Now it follows for $X_i$,
$i > 0$, using induction on $i$ and Theorem \ref{thm:K-loc}.
	
	The realization map $K'_0(X)\cong K'_0(X)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} K_0(k)\to K'_0(X_k)$ is an edge map in the K\"unneth spectral
	sequence (see \cite{Adams69}) converging to $K'_*(X_k)\cong \pi_*\left(K(k)\wedge K' (X)\right)$. Since all spectra involved are connective, the map is an isomorphism.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- rem-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:higher-comparison}
The statement of Theorem \ref{thm:comparison} applies
to general pc monoid schemes $X$, using localization and devissage.
We omit the details here, as we do not need that level of generality.
<!-- end rem-3 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:K'-descent}
	Let $X\in{\mathcal M}_{\text{pctf}}$. Then the presheaf $K'$ on $X_{\mathrm{zar}}$ satisfies descent.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
By \cite[Lemma 5.2]{CHWW-p}, this is true when $X$ is affine. Now the general case follows using Corollary \ref{cor:K'-MV}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- defn-6: body_md -->
\label{defn:K-Zar}
Let $K^Q$ be the presheaf of $K$-theory spectra on ${\mathcal M}_{\text{pctf}}$ 
defined in \cite[Section 3.4]{ELY}.
We write $K^{\mathrm{zar}}$ for the presheaf $\mathbb H_{{\mathrm{zar}}}(-, K^Q)$. For $n\in\mathbb{Z}$ we set
$K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(X) = \mathbb H_{{\mathrm{zar}}}^{-n}(X, K^Q).$
<!-- end defn-6 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:affine-equivalence}
Let $U\in {\mathcal M}_{\text{pctf}}$ be affine. Then $K^Q(U)\rightarrow K^{\mathrm{zar}} (U)$
is a weak homotopy equivalence.
Therefore $K^Q_n(U)\xrightarrow{\sim} K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(U)$
is an isomorphism for all $n$.
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:K-htpy-invariance}
	If $A$ is a pc monoid, then the natural maps
	 \[K^Q(A)\to K^Q(A\wedge \mathbb{N}_+)\quad\text{and}\quad K'(A)\to K'(A\wedge \mathbb{N}_+)\]
	 are weak homotopy equivalences.
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
The first assertion follows from \cite[Thm.\,2.6]{ELY} since the natural homomorphism of units $A^\times \to \left(A\wedge \mathbb{N}_+\right)^\times$ is an isomorphism. The second assertion is \cite[Thm.\,4.6]{HW}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- thm-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:K-vs-K'}
	Let $X$ be a smooth monoid scheme. Then the natural map
 $K^{\mathrm{zar}} (X)\xrightarrow{\sim} K'(X)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.
<!-- end thm-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Assume first that $X = \operatorname{MSpec} (A)$ is affine and smooth. In this case, $K^Q(X)\xrightarrow{\sim} K^{\mathrm{zar}}(X)$ by Lemma \ref{lem:affine-equivalence}, so we need to show that the map $K^Q(X)\to K'(X)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Since $X$ is smooth, it is a product of an affine space and a torus, in other words, $A$ is isomorphic to a smash product $\mathbb{N}_+^{\wedge s} \wedge \mathbb{Z}_+^{\wedge t}$  of a
	free pointed abelian monoid and a free pointed abelian group. Suppose that $s = 0$. Then $A$ is a (pointed) group, and thus, every pc $A$-set is automatically projective (as noted in \cite[Ex.\,1.4]{HW}). It follows that $K^Q(X) = K'(X)$.
	
	 Now suppose $s > 0$. Consider the following commutative square of $K$-theory spectra:
		\begin{equation}\label{cart-square}
		\xymatrix{
			K^Q(\mathbb{Z}_+^{\wedge t})  \ar[r]\ar[d]^{\cong}&
			K'(\mathbb{Z}_+^{\wedge t}) \ar[d]^{\cong} 
			\\
			K^Q(\mathbb{N}_+^{\wedge s} \wedge \mathbb{Z}_+^{\wedge t})  \ar[r]& K'(\mathbb{N}_+^{\wedge s} \wedge \mathbb{Z}_+^{\wedge t}).
		}
	\end{equation}
	We have just observed that the top horizontal map is a weak homotopy equivalence. Since the
	 vertical maps are weak homotopy equivalences by Lemma \ref{lem:K-htpy-invariance}, the bottom horizontal map is also a weak homotopy equivalence. 
	
	The general case now follows by Zariski descent, which holds for $K'$ by Lemma \ref{lem:K'-descent}, and for $K^{\mathrm{zar}}$ by definition.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:K_0}
	Let $X$ be a smooth monoid scheme, and $k$ a field. Then there is a natural isomorphism
	$K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)\xrightarrow{\sim} K_0(X_k)$.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Combine Theorems \ref{thm:K-vs-K'} and \ref{thm:comparison}.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:local-embedding}
	The pullback maps $i^*:K^{\mathrm{zar}}(X)\to K^{\mathrm{zar}}(Y)$ and $i'^*:K^{\mathrm{zar}}(X')\to K^{\mathrm{zar}}(Y')$ are weak
	 homotopy equivalences.
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
$K^{\mathrm{zar}}$ is homotopy invariant for vector bundles by Lemma \ref{lem:K-htpy-invariance} and Zariski descent. Now the
	 assertion follows from the observations in the two paragraphs above.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- thm-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:scdh-descent}
	Let $X$ be a smooth toric monoid scheme, $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ a smooth closed equivariant subscheme, $X'\xrightarrow{\pi} X$ the blow-up along $Y$ and $Y'\xrightarrow{\pi'} Y$ the exceptional divisor. Let $U\subseteq X$ be open,
	 and write $U' = \pi^{-1}(U)$. Then the following commutative square of spectra is homotopy cartesian:
	\begin{equation}\label{MV-square}
		\xymatrix{
			K^{\mathrm{zar}}(U)  \ar[r]^{i^*}\ar[d]^{\pi^*}&
			K^{\mathrm{zar}}(U\cap Y) \ar[d]^{\pi'^*} 
			\\
			K^{\mathrm{zar}}(U')  \ar[r]^{i'^*}& K^{\mathrm{zar}}(U'\cap Y').
		}
	\end{equation}
<!-- end thm-6 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Write $F(U) = \mathrm{hofib}(i^*\vert_U)$ and $F'(U) = \mathrm{hofib}(i'^*\vert_{\pi^{-1}(U)})$ for the (horizontal) homotopy fibers evaluated at $U$. Then $F$ and $F'$ are presheaves of spectra on $X$ satisfying Zariski descent, and the commutativity of the square induces a natural transformation $\phi:F\to F'$. Assume $V$ is affine. If $V\cap Y = \emptyset$, then $V'\to V$ is an isomorphism and $F(V)\to F'(V)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. On the other hand, if $V\cap Y\neq \emptyset$, then Lemma \ref{lem:local-embedding} implies that $F(V)\simeq \ast\simeq F'(V)$. Therefore, $\phi(V)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for all affine open $V\subseteq X$. 

By Zariski descent, $F(U)\to F'(U)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for all open $U\subseteq X$. That is, \eqref{MV-square} is homotopy cartesian.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- thm-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:proj-bundle-formula}
	Let $n\geq 0$ and $r\geq 0$. The natural homomorphism $\phi^r$ of \eqref{phi-defn} is an
	 isomorphism:
	\[\mathbb{Z}^{S}\otimes_\mathbb{Z} K'_n(X)\xrightarrow{\phi^r} K'_n(\mathbb{P}).\]
	 Equivalently, 
	 there are natural isomorphisms, 
	\[\phi^E:K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(\mathbb{P})\otimes_{K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)} K'_n(X)\to K'_n(\mathbb{P}).\]
<!-- end thm-7 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:proj-space}
	Let $n,\,r\geq 0.$ Then the map $\phi^r$ of \eqref{phi-defn} is an isomorphism
		\[\mathbb{Z}^{S}\otimes_\mathbb{Z} K'_n(\mathbf{pt})\xrightarrow{\sim} K'_n(\mathbb{P}^r).\]
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
For any field $k$, $K_0(\mathbb{P}^r_k)$ is isomorphic to $A_r = \mathbb{Z}[t]/(t^{r+1})$ as a ring, where $t = 1-z$. 
	We regard $\phi^r$ as a map $A_r\otimes_\mathbb{Z} K'_n(\mathbf{pt})\to K'_n(\mathbb{P}^{r})$. 
	To prove that $\phi^r$ is an isomorphism for all $r$, we proceed by induction on $r\geq 0$. 
	
  The assertion is trivial if $r = 0$. Suppose now that $r > 0$ and we have proved that $\phi^{r-1}: A_{r-1}\otimes_\mathbb{Z} K'_n(\mathbf{pt})\to K'_n(\mathbb{P}^{r-1})$ is an isomorphism. Recall from \cite{HW} that $K'_n(\mathbf{pt}) \cong \pi^s_n$, the $n$-th stable stem. 
  
  Let $\mathbb{P}^{r-1}\xrightarrow{i} \mathbb{P}^r$ be the usual closed immersion, and $\mathbb{A}^r\xrightarrow{j} \mathbb{P}^r$ the complementary open immersion. Consider the following (not obviously commutative) diagram:
	\begin{equation}\label{projective-ladder}
		\xymatrix{
			0  \ar[r]&
			A_{r-1}\otimes_\mathbb{Z} \pi^s_n \ar[d]^{\phi^{r-1}} \ar[r]^{t\cdot}& A_r\otimes_\mathbb{Z} \pi^s_n \ar[d]^{\phi^r} \ar[r]^{ev_0}& \pi^s_n \ar[d]^{\lambda^*} \ar[r]& 0
			\\
			0  \ar[r]&
			K'_n(\mathbb{P}^{r-1}) \ar[r]^{i_*}& K'_n(\mathbb{P}^r) \ar[r]^{j^*}& K'_n(\mathbb{A}^r) \ar[r]& 0
		}
	\end{equation}
	
	The first vertical map $\phi^{r-1}$ is an isomorphism by induction, and the third vertical map $\pi^s_n \cong K'_n(\mathbf{pt})\to K'_n(\mathbb{A}^r)$ is given by flat pullback, which is an isomorphism by the homotopy invariance of $K'_\ast$. The top row in this diagram is (split) exact. 
	
	The composition of flat pullbacks $K'_n(\mathbf{pt})\to K'_n(\mathbb{P}^r)\to K'_n(\mathbb{A}^r)$ is an isomorphism by homotopy invariance, and thus the restriction map $j^*:K'_n(\mathbb{P}^r)\to K'_n(\mathbb{A}^r)$ is split surjective for all $n\geq 0$; it follows that the bottom row of the diagram is (split) exact for all $n$ as well. To conclude the proof, it therefore suffices to show that the diagram \eqref{projective-ladder} commutes. 
	
	Consider the left-hand square first. Unravelling definitions, we must show the following:
	
	\noindent{\it Claim:} Write $q_r:\mathbb{P}^r\to \mathbf{pt}$ and $q_{r-1}: \mathbb{P}^{r-1}\to \mathbf{pt}$ for the structure maps, and $i:\mathbb{P}^{r-1}\to\mathbb{P}^r$ for the closed immersion. Let $k$ be a field, $y\in K_0(\mathbb{P}^{r-1}_k)\cong K'_0(\mathbb{P}^{r-1})$, and $\alpha\in K'_n(\mathbf{pt})$. Then
	\[ i_*(y\cup q_{r-1}^*(\alpha)) = i_*(y)\cup q_r^*(\alpha). \]
	Indeed, this is a special case of Lemma \ref{lem:projection_formula_1} below. 
	
	Now consider the right-hand square of \eqref{projective-ladder}, writing $ev_0$ for the evaluation at $0$ map and $\lambda:\mathbb{A}^r\to \mathbf{pt}$ for the structure map, so that the right vertical isomorphism acts on $\alpha\in\pi^s_n\cong K'_n(\mathbf{pt})$ as $\alpha\mapsto \lambda^*(\alpha)$. We have to show that $j^*\circ\phi^r = \lambda^*\circ ev_0$. By commutativity of the left square, both composites are zero on elements of the form $t^m\otimes\alpha$ with $m > 0$. If $m = 0$, then by functoriality of flat pullback:
	$j^*(\phi^r(1\otimes\alpha))  = j^* (q_r^*(\alpha)) = \lambda^*(\alpha)$
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
Write $q_r:\mathbb{P}^r\to \mathbf{pt}$ and $q_{r-1}: \mathbb{P}^{r-1}\to \mathbf{pt}$ for the structure maps, and $i:\mathbb{P}^{r-1}\to\mathbb{P}^r$ for the closed immersion. Let $k$ be a field, $y\in K_0(\mathbb{P}^{r-1}_k)\cong K'_0(\mathbb{P}^{r-1})$, and $\alpha\in K'_n(\mathbf{pt})$. Then
	\[ i_*(y\cup q_{r-1}^*(\alpha)) = i_*(y)\cup q_r^*(\alpha). \]
	Indeed, this is a special case of Lemma \ref{lem:projection_formula_1} below.
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
As observed in \cite[4.3]{Quillen}, the assertions that $\phi^r$ and $\phi^E$ are isomorphisms are equivalent. Consider the presheaves of sequences of abelian groups on $X$ sending $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ to the sequences 
	\[\mathbf{A}_n(U) = \mathbb{Z}^{S}\otimes_\mathbb{Z} K'_n(U)\; \text{and}\; 
	\mathbf{B}_n(U) = K'_n(\mathbb{P}(j^* E))\]
	 in the theorem, respectively. Then $\phi^r$ induces a natural transformation between these presheaves. 
	
	Since $\mathbb{Z}^{S}$ is a free abelian group, Corollary \ref{cor:K'-MV} implies that $\mathbf{A}_*$ has a long exact Mayer-Vietoris sequence for open covers. By the same result, $\mathbf{B}_*$ satisfies Mayer-Vietoris since, for an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, $\mathbb{P}(j^* E)\to \mathbb{P}(E)$ is also an open immersion. Using induction on the cardinality of an affine open cover of $X$, we reduce to the case where $X$ is affine. Now since $X$ is smooth, 
	$X = \operatorname{MSpec}(\mathbb{N}_+^{\wedge s}\wedge \mathbb{Z}_+^{\wedge t})$. This implies in particular that $p:E\to X$ is a trivial vector bundle. Applying homotopy invariance and the Fundamental Theorem \cite[Theorem 4.6]{HW}, we can further reduce to the case where $X$ is a point, so that $\mathbb{P}(E) \cong \mathbb{P}^{r}$. Now Proposition \ref{prop:proj-space} applies to finish the proof.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- thm-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:K-of-sm-proj}
  Let $X$ be a smooth proper toric monoid scheme, and $k$ a field.
  Then $K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)$ is a free abelian group, and the natural map
  of \eqref{eqn:K_0-action} is a weak homotopy equivalence.
  Equivalently, the natural homomorphisms 
  \[ \mu^X_n: K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} \pi^s_n
  = K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(\mathbf{pt}) \xrightarrow{\sim} K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(X)
  \]
are isomorphisms for all $n\geq 0$.
<!-- end thm-8 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:factorization}
		Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be smooth proper toric monoid schemes of the same dimension. Then there exists a smooth proper toric monoid scheme $\widetilde{X}$ and morphisms $f_1:\widetilde{X}\to X_1$ and $f_2:\widetilde{X}\to X_2$ such that $f_1$ and $f_2$ are compositions of blow-ups along smooth closed equivariant subschemes.
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
The fans of $X_1$ and $X_2$ are both regular and complete by
assumption. Thus, they satisfy the hypotheses of
\cite[Thm.\,A]{Wlodarczyk}. Now the assertion follows by applying the
functor from fans to toric monoid schemes of Definition
\ref{fan-monoid-scheme}.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:single-blow-up}
  Assume that $K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(Y)$ is free abelian and the map $\mu^Y_n$
  of \eqref{eqn:K_0-action} is an isomorphism for all $n\geq 0$. \\
  Then $K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)$ is free and $\mu^X_n$ is an isomorphism for all
  $n\geq 0$ if, and only if, $K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X')$ is free and
  $\mu^{X'}_n$ is an isomorphism for all $n\geq 0$.
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
It follows from the hypothesis on $Y$ and the projective bundle
formula (Theorem \ref{thm:proj-bundle-formula}) that
$K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(Y')$ is free, and
$\mu^{Y'}_n$ is an isomorphism for all $n\geq 0$.
By \cite[Thm.\,2.1]{T} and Corollary \ref{cor:K_0},
\[K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X')\cong K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)\oplus K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(Y)^{\oplus (c-1)},\]
where $c$ is the codimension of $Y$ in $X$.
Since $K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(Y)$ is assumed free, it follows that
$K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)$ is free if, and only if, $K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X')$ is. 
	
Let $k$ be a field. Then \cite[Lem.\,2.3]{T} implies that 
\[K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)\cong K_0(X_k)\to K_0(X'_k)\cong K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X')\]
is a split injection. Since $Y$ is smooth, $K_{-1}(Y_k) = 0$.
Therefore the Mayer-Vietoris sequence
\begin{equation}\label{MV-split} 
0\to K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)\to K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(Y)\oplus K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X')\to K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(Y')\to 0 
\end{equation}
is split exact. 
	
Now consider the following diagram, where $n\geq 0$:
\begin{equation*}\xymatrix{
K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)\otimes_\mathbb{Z} \pi^s_n \ar[d]^{\mu^X_n} \ar[r]^{\mathrm{into}}&
\left(\underset{K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(Y)}{\overset{K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X')}{\oplus}}\right)
\otimes_\mathbb{Z} \pi^s_n \ar[d]^{\mu^Y_n\oplus\mu^{X'}_n} \ar[r]& K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(Y')\otimes_\mathbb{Z}\pi^s_n \ar[d]^{\mu^{Y'}_n} \ar[r]& 0
			\\
K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(X) \ar[r]& \left(\underset{K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(Y)}{\overset{K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(X')}{\oplus}}\right) \ar[r]&K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(Y') \ar[r]^{\delta_n}& K^{\mathrm{zar}}_{n-1}(X) 
}
\end{equation*}

The bottom row is a piece of the long exact Mayer-Vietoris sequence
associated to the homotopy cartesian square \eqref{MV-square},
and the top row is the split exact sequence \eqref{MV-split},
tensored with $K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(\mathbf{pt}) = \pi^s_n$.
The diagram commutes, since the action of Corollary \ref{cor:vb-action}
is natural. We observed above that, for all $n\geq 0$,
the right vertical homomorphism $\mu^{Y'}_n$ is an isomorphism; it follows by an easy diagram chase that $\delta_n = 0$, and thus the sequence
\[
  0\to K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(X)\to K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(Y)\oplus K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(X')\to K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(Y')\to 0
\]
is short exact for all $n\geq 0$ as well.
Now the Five Lemma implies that $\mu_n^X$ is an isomorphism
exactly when
$\mu_n^{X'}$ is.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
We proceed by induction on $d = \dim (X)$. If $d = 0$,
then $X = \mathbf{pt}$ and the assertion is straightforward.
Now let $d > 0$, and assume we have proved that $K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(Y)$ is a
free abelian group and the map $\mu^Y$ of \eqref{eqn:K_0-action}
  is a weak homotopy equivalence for all smooth proper toric
  monoid schemes $Y$ of dimension less than $d$. 
		
  By Proposition \ref{prop:factorization}, there is a smooth proper
  toric monoid scheme $\tilde{X}$ and morphisms $\tilde{X}\to X$
  and $\tilde{X}\to\mathbb{P}^d$ that are compositions of blow-ups
  along smooth closed equivariant subschemes. Now $\mu^{\mathbb{P}}$,
  where $\mathbb{P} = \mathbb{P}^d$, is a weak homotopy equivalence by
  Proposition \ref{prop:proj-space}, and $K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(\mathbb{P}^d)$ is
  free of rank $d+1$. 
  By induction on the number of blow-ups needed in the factorization,
  we conclude (using  Proposition \ref{prop:single-blow-up}) that
  $K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)$ is a free abelian group, and that $\mu^X_n$ is an
  isomorphism for all $n\geq 0$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- rem-4: body_md -->
Using Theorem \ref{thm:comparison}, this provides
  an alternative proof for the proper case of
  Vezzosi and Vistoli \cite[Cor.\,6.10]{VV}.
<!-- end rem-4 -->
<!-- defn-7: body_md -->
\label{lin-flat-defn}
A matroid is a set $E$ together with a collection 
$\mathcal F$ of subsets called ``flats" satisfying the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $E\in\mathcal F$.  
\item[(ii)] $F,G\in\mathcal F$ implies $F\cap G\in\mathcal F$.
\item[(iii)] If $F$ is a flat, and $x\in E\setminus F$, 
  then there is a unique flat $F'$ minimal over $F$ containing $x$. 
	\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-7 -->
<!-- ex-4: body_md -->
\label{ex:uniform} 
Let $E=\{1,2,...,n\}$ and $m\le n$. In the 
{\it uniform matroid} $U_{m,n}$ (see \cite[1.2.7]{Ox})
the flats are all subsets of $E$ having cardinality
less than $m$, and the whole set.
<!-- end ex-4 -->
<!-- defn-8: body_md -->
\label{Bergman}  (\cite[3.10]{Huh})
	Given a loopless matroid $(E,\mathcal F)$ of rank $r+1$, 
	the {\it Bergman fan} $\Delta_{\mathcal F}$
	is the $r$-dimensional fan in $N=\mathbb{Z}^{|E|}/(1,...,1)$ whose cones
	$\sigma_{\mathcal F}$ correspond to
	flags of nonempty proper flats of $(E,\mathcal F)$.
	\[
	\mathcal F = (F_1 \subset F_2 \subset \cdots \subset F_d).
	\]
	More precisely, fix a bijection $E \cong \{0,1,\dotsc, n\}$ and let 
	\[
	\mathbf{u}_0=(1,0,\dots,0),...,\mathbf{u}_n=(0,\dots,0,1)\quad \text{in~}\, \mathbb{Z}^{n+1}.
	\]
	be the $n+1$ standard unit vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^{n+1}.$
	
	For a subset $S$ of $E = \{0,\dotsc, n\}$, let $\mathbf{u}_S\in N$ be the
	image of the vector $\sum_{i\in S} \mathbf{u}_i$. Then the cone associated to
	the flag $\mathcal F$ is spanned by $\{\mathbf{u}_{F_1},\dotsc, \mathbf{u}_{F_d}\}.$ In
	particular, the set of rays of the Bergman fan is in one-to-one
	correspondence with the set of flats of the matroid.
	
	If $E$ is not loopless,  write $E=E'\amalg E''$,
	where $E'$ is loopless and $E''$ is the set of loops in $E$.
	Then the Bergman fan of $E$ is defined as the product of the
	Bergman fan of $E'$, and the fan corresponding to the
	one-point monoid scheme $\operatorname{MSpec}(\mathbb{Z}^r)$, with $r=|E'']$.
<!-- end defn-8 -->
<!-- defn-9: body_md -->
\label{defn:permutahedron}
	(See \cite[3.2]{Huh}.)
	The $n$-dimensional permutohedral fan in
	$N=\mathbb{Z}^{n+1}/\text{span}(1,1,\dots,1)$ is the complete fan
	whose cones are spanned by $\{\mathbf{u}_{S_1}, \cdots, \mathbf{u}_{S_d}\}$,
	where 
	\[\emptyset\subset S_1\subset S_2 \subset \dotsm \subset S_d\subset \{0,1,\dotsc, n\}\]
	 is a flag of proper, non-empty subsets. 
This is the Bergman fan of the Boolean matroid $U_{n+1,n+1}$.
<!-- end defn-9 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{bergman-fans-smooth}
The toric monoid scheme 
associated to the Bergman fan of a matroid $(E,\mathcal F)$ is smooth and
quasiprojective.
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- ex-5: body_md -->
\label{ex:K-of-boolean}
	Fix an integer $n\geq 2$. For all $m\geq 0$, we have
	\[K_0(U_{n,n})\otimes_\mathbb{Z}\pi_m^s\xrightarrow{\sim} K_m(U_{n,n}).\]
	 Moreover, $K_0(U_{n,n}) = \mathbb{Z}[\{x_F\}, F\in \mathcal{P}_n]$, where $\mathcal{P}_n$ is the set of non-empty proper subsets of $\{1,2,\dotsc, n\}.$ Thus, the elements of $\mathcal{P}_n$ are in one-to-one correspondence with the rays of the
		 $(n-1)$-dimensional permutohedral fan. The generators $x_F$ satisfy the following list of relations:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $1 - \displaystyle\prod_{F} (1 - x_F)$;
		\item $1 - \displaystyle\prod_{i\notin F} (1 - x_F)$, for $i = 1,\dotsc, n$;
		\item $x_F x_G$, for all incomparable subsets $F$ and $G$ of $\{1,\dotsc, n\}.$ 
	\end{enumerate}
<!-- end ex-5 -->
<!-- ex-6: body_md -->
\label{ex:K-of-U_{2,3}}
Consider the matroid $U_{2,3}$, with $E=\{0,1,2\}$. As indicated in
Example \ref{ex:uniform}, its flats are $\emptyset$, the one-elements
subsets $\{0\}$, $\{1\}$ and $\{2\}$, and $\{0,1,2\}$. It follows that
the only proper flats are the singletons, and the Bergman fan of
$U_{2,3}$ is the fan in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with rays $\mathbf{u}_1$, $\mathbf{u}_2$, and $\mathbf{u}_0
= -\mathbf{u}_1 - \mathbf{u}_2$, and has no two-dimensional cones. The associated toric
monoid scheme is the complement $V$ of the three closed points in
$\mathbb{P}^2$.  Since $V$ is smooth, $K_n(U_{2,3}) = K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(V)\cong
K'_n(V)$.

To determine the groups $K'_n(V)$, we first note that the push-forward
$K'(\mathbf{pt})\xrightarrow{i_*} K'(\mathbb{P}^2)$ does not depend on the closed
point. Theorem \ref{thm:K-loc} implies that there is a long exact
sequence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:U32-sequence}
	 \dotsc\to K'_n(\mathbf{pt})^{\oplus 3}\xrightarrow{\oplus i_*} K'_n(\mathbb{P}^2)\to K'_n(V) \to K'_{n-1}(\mathbf{pt})^{\oplus 3}\to \dotsc 
\end{equation}
It follows from the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:proj-space} that
$K'_n(\mathbf{pt})\xrightarrow{i_*} K'_n(\mathbb{P}^2)$ is a composition of split
injective maps, and hence is split injective; therefore, the long
exact sequence \eqref{eq:U32-sequence} splits into short exact
sequences
\[
0\to K'_n(\mathbb{P}^2)/i_* \left(K'_n(\mathbf{pt})\right) \to K'_n(V)\to K'_{n-1}(\mathbf{pt})^{\oplus 2}\to 0.
\]
Applying Proposition \ref{prop:proj-space}, we can express
$K_n(U_{2,3}) = K'_n(V)$ as an
extension of stable homotopy groups of spheres:
\[
0\to (\pi_n^s)^{\oplus 2} \to K_n(U_{2,3})\to (\pi_{n-1}^s)^{\oplus 2}\to 0.
\]
<!-- end ex-6 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:K_is_ring}
  Let $X$ be a pctf monoid scheme. The spectrum $K^Q(X)$
  has the natural structure of an $E_\infty$-ring spectrum,
  and $K'(X)$ is a module over $K^Q(X)$.
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
In particular, a quasi-exact category has the structure of a
Waldhausen category, where the cofibrations are admissible
monomorphisms and the weak equivalences are isomorphisms. It is
well-known (see \cite[1.9]{Waldhausen1126}) that the $K$-theory (via the
$wS_\bullet$-construction) of this Waldhausen category is equivalent
to the $K$-theory of the original quasi-exact category (via the
$Q$-construction). Now we can apply Barwick's result.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- lem-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:Kzar-as-finite-limit}
  Let $X$ be a separated pctf monoid scheme of finite type, and $\{U_i\}$
  a (finite) cover by affine open subschemes. Write $\mathcal{U}_\bullet$
  for the associated (\u{C}ech) simplicial scheme.
  Then we have a canonical weak homotopy equivalence
\[ K^{\mathrm{zar}}(X)\to \mathrm{lim}_{\Delta} K^{\mathrm{zar}} (\mathcal{U}_\bullet)
\simeq \mathrm{lim}_{\Delta} K^Q(\mathcal{U}_\bullet).
\]
<!-- end lem-6 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
The first statement is a consequence of the fact that $K^{\mathrm{zar}}$ is a
sheaf in the Zariski topology, which is true by construction. Now the
second assertion follows from Lemma \ref{lem:affine-equivalence}.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:Kzar-is-ring}
  Let $X$ be a separated pctf monoid scheme of finite type.
Then $K^{\mathrm{zar}}(X)$ has the natural structure of an $E_\infty$-ring spectrum. 
	
When $X$ is affine, the $E_\infty$ ring structure is transported from
$K^Q(X)$ via the weak homotopy equivalence $K^Q(X)\to
K^{\mathrm{zar}}(X)$. Moreover, $K'(X)$ is a module over $K^{\mathrm{zar}}(X)$.
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
As the forgetful functor to spectra commutes with limits,
  the first assertion follows from Lemmas \ref{lem:K_is_ring}
  and \ref{lem:Kzar-as-finite-limit}.

  It also follows from Lemma \ref{lem:K_is_ring} that
  $\mathbb H_{\mathrm{zar}}(X,K')$ is a module over $K^{\mathrm{zar}}(X)$. Since the
  presheaf $K'$ satisfies descent on $X_{\mathrm{zar}}$ by Lemma \ref{lem:K'-descent}, the second assertion follows.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:vb-action}
  Let $X$ be a smooth toric monoid scheme of finite type, $k$ a field,
  and $n\geq 0$. Then $K^{\mathrm{zar}}_n(X)$ and $K'_n(X)$ have natural
  module structures over the commutative ring $K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0(X)\cong K_0(X_k)$.
  In particular, every vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on $X_k$
  determines a homomorphism $[\mathcal{E}]\cup - : K'_n(X) \to K'_n(X)$.
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Combine Proposition \ref{prop:Kzar-is-ring}, Theorem \ref{thm:comparison} and Theorem \ref{thm:K-vs-K'}.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lem-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:projection_formula_1}
	There is an identity of functors 
	\[\wedge_X\circ (i_*\times\mathrm{id}) = i_* \circ \wedge_Y:  \mathbf{Sh}_Y\times\mathbf{Sets}_*\to \mathbf{Sh}_X.\]
	 Therefore, if $y\in K^{\mathrm{zar}}_0 (Y)$, and $\alpha\in K'_n(\mathbf{pt})$, then
	\[ i_*(y)\cup q_X^*(\alpha)=i_*(y\cup q_Y^*(\alpha)).\]
<!-- end lem-7 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
The first identity follows by inspection. To conclude the second
identity, observe that, viewed as functions on pairs $(y,\alpha)$, the
left--hand side is induced by the functor $\wedge_X\circ
(i_*\times\mathrm{id})$, and the right--hand side by the functor $i_*
\circ \wedge_Y$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:algebras}
 	 The map
 	\[ (R\otimes\mathbf{A})\wedge (R\otimes\mathbf{A})\xrightarrow{\sim} (R\otimes_\mathbb{Z} R)\otimes (\mathbf{A}\wedge\mathbf{A})\xrightarrow{m\otimes\mu} R\otimes\mathbf{A},\]
 	induced by the products on $R$ and $\mathbf{A},$
 	makes $R\otimes\mathbf{A}$ a commutative ring in $\mathfrak{C}$.
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
As explained in \cite[Sec.\,6]{Pa}, the functor $\otimes$ is
(strongly) monoidal in the first variable. It is now straightforward
(if tedious) to check that the operation given in the assertion endows
$R\otimes \mathbf{A}$ with the structure of a commutative ring in
$\mathfrak{C}$. In a much more general context this is proved, for
example, as part of \cite[Cor.\,3.6]{Sch}.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- cor-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:algebras}
$R\otimes\mathbf{E}$ has a natural structure of
commutative ring spectrum such that the following
natural map of graded rings is an isomorphism:
\[
R\otimes_\mathbb{Z} \pi_* (\mathbf{E})   \xrightarrow{\sim}
\pi_*(R\otimes\mathbf{E})
\]
<!-- end cor-4 -->
